title: Neurological warning signs
summary: Sudden speech disturbance, facial asymmetry, weakness on one side, sudden loss of vision or a sudden severe headache may indicate an acute neurological event. Stroke or TIA must be ruled out when focal signs are present, even if they have already resolved. A headache without those signs is assessed in its own context or through the cabin route. Informational support only: not a diagnosis or a treatment decision. There are no clinical personnel on board: the steps are first aid and monitoring; treatment depends on mission procedures.

immediate.text: Possible stroke signs: emergency, even if the signs have already resolved.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Call for emergency help now using the mission's means (ship alarm, crew, mission control if the link is up). Do not wait to see if it improves.
Note the time the first symptoms started.
Another crew member: do the B.E. F.A.S.T. check (balance, eyes, face, arms, speech) and note the time.

missing_guidance: The card's sources do not give onboard treatment: it depends on the mission procedure.

headache_check.text: Headache with unknown onset and severity: check for neurological warning signs.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Check: did it start suddenly and is it very severe? Is it hard to speak, is your vision impaired, is one side of your face drooping, or are you losing strength on one side? If so, treat it as an emergency.

questions.headache_red_flags: Did the headache start suddenly and is it very severe, or does it come with speech disturbance, facial drooping, weakness on one side or loss of vision?

candidates.label: Stroke or transient ischemic attack (must be ruled out)
candidates.minimum_evidence: At least one sudden focal sign (speech, face, weakness on one side, vision) or a sudden severe headache, current or already resolved.

sources.title: CDC: Signs and Symptoms of Stroke
